overview.intro:
Chapter 23 covers what the food industry leaves behind and what animals eat — **dog and cat food**, prepared livestock feed, soybean and canola meal, fish and meat meal, bran, beet pulp and distillers' grains. Its **61 tariff lines** carry small printed rates: 25 are Free, most others are 1.4% or a fraction of a cent per kilogram. The one steep rate is on **feed containing milk** above its quota: 80.4¢/kg + 6.4%.

So the extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a Section 301 tariff: **+12.5% on Thai and Vietnamese pet food**, +10% for Indonesia, Cambodia and Malaysia, 10% in total for the EU, and **37.5% on Chinese pet food** (+25% from 2019 plus 12.5%). USMCA-qualifying feed from Canada and Mexico enters free. The U.S. imported $5.42B of Chapter 23 goods in 2025, $3.49B of it pet food and feed preparations.

productGroups.blurb: Meat meal, greaves and fish meal are Free at base. The cost is the Section 301 duty for the country and the APHIS permit that animal-protein meals need.

productGroups.label: Bran & milling residues

productGroups.label: Starch residues, beet pulp & distillers' grains
productGroups.blurb: Corn gluten feed and meal pay 1.4%; beet pulp, bagasse and brewers' or distillers' grains are Free.

productGroups.label: Soybean meal
productGroups.blurb: Soybean meal and cake pay 0.45¢/kg — about $4.50 a tonne — with a separate statistical line for certified organic meal.

productGroups.label: Canola, sunflower & other oilcake

productGroups.label: Wine lees
productGroups.blurb: Wine lees and argol (crude tartar) are Free.

productGroups.label: Acorns, citrus pulp & other plant feed
productGroups.blurb: Acorns and citrus pulp pellets pay 1.4%, dehydrated marigolds 1.9%; grain screenings and chaff are Free.

productGroups.label: Pet food & prepared animal feed

workedExamples.title: A container of canned cat food from Thailand
workedExamples.body: Dog or cat food for retail sale is Free at base. Thailand is one of the 60 economies in the 2026 Section 301 action, so 12.5% of value is added (9903.05.77): on an $80,000 container that is **$10,000**. The same container from a USMCA-qualifying Canadian plant pays **$0**.

workedExamples.title: 1,000 tonnes of canola meal from Canada
workedExamples.body: Low-erucic rapeseed (canola) meal is 0.17¢/kg: 1,000,000 kg × $0.0017 = **$1,700** base duty, which a USMCA claim makes Free. Meal that doesn't qualify for USMCA also pays 10% of value under Section 301 (9903.05.29) — **$35,000** more at $350 a tonne.

workedExamples.title: $50,000 of dry dog food from China
workedExamples.body: Free at base, but Chinese pet food is on Section 301 List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) and the 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.31): 37.5% × $50,000 = **$18,750**. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

workedExamples.title: 20 tonnes of milk replacer from Ireland
workedExamples.body: Inside the quota (Ireland's share is 5,470,323 kg a year) the rate is 7.5%, which the EU Section 301 rule tops up to 10%: **$6,000** on $60,000. Once the quota is full the same feed enters under 2309.90.28 at 80.4¢/kg + 6.4%: 20,000 × $0.804 + 6.4% × $60,000 = **$19,920**.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Heading 2309 includes products of a kind used in animal feeding, not elsewhere specified or included, obtained by processing vegetable or animal materials to such an extent that they have lost the essential characteristics of the original material, other than vegetable waste, vegetable residues and byproducts of such processing.

**Subheading note 1.** For subheading 2306.41, "low erucic acid rape or colza seeds" means seeds as defined in subheading note 1 to chapter 12.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Note 1.** "Mixed feeds and mixed-feed ingredients" in subheading 2309.90.10 are products of heading 2309 that are admixtures of grains (or products, including byproducts, obtained in milling grains) with molasses, oilcake, oil-cake meal or feedstuffs, and that consist of not less than 6 percent by weight of grain or grain products.

**Note 2.** Animal feed containing milk or milk derivatives entered under subheadings 2309.90.24 and 2309.90.44 may not exceed 7,399,700 kg in any calendar year (products of Mexico are not included). Ireland has access to at least 5,470,323 kg, New Zealand 1,782,618 kg, the United Kingdom 83,914 kg and Australia 56,699 kg.

seo.shortDescription: Every 2025–2026 tariff change for HTS Chapter 23 with dates and official sources: IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, Section 301 duties of 10%–37.5% since July 2026, lysine antidumping duties on China.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 23 base rate changed** — all 61 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates.

Everything happened on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended on **February 24, 2026**; a 10% Section 122 surcharge replaced them until **July 23, 2026**. Since **July 24, 2026** goods of 60 economies pay a Section 301 duty — +12.5% for Thailand and Vietnam, +10% for Indonesia, Cambodia and Malaysia, 10% in total for the EU — and Brazil pays 37.5%. China pays 12.5% on top of its older 25% or 7.5% lists, and since **September 16, 2026** feed-grade lysine from China also owes antidumping and countervailing duties. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico stay exempt.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 23 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the older China Section 301 lists, the Nicaragua Section 301 tariff that starts in 2027, the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended, the 2026 antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese lysine, and FDA import rules that changed. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods entered free under USMCA pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). No Chapter 23 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)). Milk-based feed over the quota (2309.90.28, 2309.90.48) is free under USMCA only within Canada's 696.9 t quota for 2026 (9823.05.02), shared with whole milk powder. The 35% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods ended February 24, 2026, and the 2026 Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles name no Chapter 23 line.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying canola meal, soybean meal and pet food from Canada pay $0. Goods that don't qualify pay their base rate plus 10% of value: on a $350,000 shipment of canola meal that is $35,000 more. Canada shipped $1.82B of Chapter 23 goods in 2025, $1.0B of it canola and other oilcake.

inEffect.whatItMeans: Thai pet food has a Free base rate, so the whole bill is the Section 301 duty: 12.5% of value, or $10,000 on an $80,000 container of canned cat food. Thailand was the No. 2 supplier in 2025 ($1.04B, almost all pet food and feed preparations).

inEffect.exemption: Coconut or copra oilcake (2306.50) is on Indonesia's exception list and pays no Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(j)(11), 9903.06.16); the other 60 lines pay +10%. The IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indonesian pet food and feed pay 10% of value on top of the base rate; copra cake (2306.50) pays only its base rate. Indonesia shipped $227M in 2025, nearly all of it heading 2309.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods entered free under USMCA pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94); Mexican milk-based feed is free under USMCA without a quota (9823.05.01). No Chapter 23 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)). The 25% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Mexican goods ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying Mexican pet food and feed enter free, including milk-based feed (9823.05.01). Goods that don't qualify pay the base rate plus 10% of value.

inEffect.exemption: No exclusion covers Chapter 23. The older lists still apply: 41 lines (pet food, most feed preparations, meat and fish meal, soybean meal, corn gluten, distillers' grains) are on List 3 at +25% (9903.88.03), and 20 lines (corn bran, cottonseed, coconut and palm-kernel cake, wine lees, milk- and egg-based feed) on List 4A at +7.5% (9903.88.15), kept in force after USTR's statutory four-year review (notice of October 7, 2026). Feed-grade lysine also owes antidumping and countervailing duties since September 2026 (see below). The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

The IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 23 goods were flat in 2025 — **$5.42B, down 0.7%** — but the mix moved. **Pet food grew**: dog and cat food for retail sale (2309.10) rose 8.5% to $2.40B, and other feed preparations (2309.90) 5.8% to $1.08B. **Canola meal**, nearly all from Canada, **fell 24.8% to $988M**, and Canada's total fell 19.8% to $1.82B. Soybean meal rose 27.1% to $500M, from Canada, Togo, Türkiye, Nigeria and India.

Pet food is where the suppliers changed. **Thailand grew 21.4% to $1.04B**, Indonesia 32.7% to $227M and Cambodia 50% to $139M, while **China fell 42.6% to $156M** — in a year when Chinese pet food paid the 25% Section 301 List 3 duty plus the 2025 IEEPA duties on China. Since July 24, 2026 Thai pet food pays 12.5% and Indonesian, Cambodian and Malaysian 10%, against 37.5% for China, so the gap between China and Southeast Asia is still there. Canada and Mexico ship mostly USMCA-qualifying goods, which have been exempt from every extra duty. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Mexican goods are Free (9823.05.01); Canadian goods are Free within a 696.9 t quota for 2026 shared with whole milk powder (9823.05.02) and 80.4¢/kg + 6.4% above it (9823.05.05, 9823.05.06).

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not in the matrix: feed-grade lysine from China (including lysine in premixes under 2309.90.70 and 2309.90.95) owes cash deposits of 73.37%–139.65% plus 48.21%–82.11% since September 2026.
The rate is not the only gate: FDA prior notice, food-facility registration and the importer's FSVP apply to all animal food, and animal-protein meals and pet food with meat need APHIS clearance.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 23: Food Industry Residues and Prepared Animal Feed — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Pet Food & Animal Feed into the U.S.: FDA & APHIS Rules, Permits & Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 23) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The documents and rules for each HTS Chapter 23 line — FDA food-facility registration, prior notice, FSVP and preventive controls for animal food, APHIS permits for meat and fish meal — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, FTA claims, the dairy-feed quota, rulings and drawback.
keywords: importing pet food into the us

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 23 goods are **food for animals**, so FDA treats them like food. The importer needs a **Foreign Supplier Verification Program**, every shipment needs **FDA prior notice**, and the foreign plant must be **registered with FDA** and follow its animal-food safety rules. Anything made from animals — meat and bone meal, fish meal, pet food with meat — also goes through **USDA APHIS**, which uses permits and BSE (mad cow disease) rules to decide whether it can enter at all.

Most of the duty comes from the extra duty by country, not the base rate. The ways to pay less are a **USMCA** claim on goods from Canada or Mexico, an **FTA** claim on the lines that still carry a base rate, and the **in-quota lines** for milk-based feed. Each one depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on feed and pet food from Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian or Mexican goods, plus any base rate (up to 1.9%, or 7.5% on in-quota milk-based feed)
levers.appliesTo: All 61 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA. Milk-based feed (2309.90.28, 2309.90.48) has its own USMCA rule: see the caveat.
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer. It need not follow a prescribed format; it can be on the invoice or another document, and CBP can ask for it.
levers.caveat: For milk-based feed outside the quota (2309.90.28, 2309.90.48), the USMCA rate is set in Chapter 98. Mexican goods are Free (9823.05.01). Canadian goods are Free only within Canada's USMCA quota, which they share with whole milk powder (696.9 t in 2026; 9823.05.02, U.S. note 5(b)(1) to subchapter XXIII), and pay 80.4¢/kg + 6.4% above it (9823.05.05, 9823.05.06). A claim without a valid certification exposes the entry to the 10% Section 301 duty plus penalties. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: USTR statement on the USMCA joint review (July 1, 2026)

levers.title: Claim a free trade agreement on the lines that carry a base rate
levers.saves: The base rate: 1.4% or 1.9% of value, 0.12¢–0.56¢/kg on oilcake, or 7.5% on in-quota milk-based feed. The Section 301 duty for the country still applies.
levers.appliesTo: Lines whose Special column lists the agreement (AU, BH, CL, CO, IL, JO, KR, MA, OM, P, PA, PE, SG); the 25 Free lines have nothing to save
levers.document: A claim on the entry with the agreement's certification or origin information — for example Chile (19 CFR 10.410), CAFTA-DR (19 CFR 10.583) or Australia (19 CFR 10.703).
levers.caveat: An FTA claim does not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a) to Chapter 99 subchapter III). On over-quota milk-based feed, Australia's FTA rate is set in Chapter 98 (9822.04.20, within Australia's FTA quantity). GSP (A, A*, A+) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Enter milk-based feed under the in-quota lines
levers.saves: 80.4¢/kg + 6.4% drops to 7.5% of value (10% in total for EU goods, which pay the Section 301 top-up). On 20 t of milk replacer worth $60,000: $19,920 over quota against $4,500 in quota ($6,000 from the EU).
levers.appliesTo: Animal feed containing milk or milk derivatives (2309.90.24 and 2309.90.44 in quota; 2309.90.28 and 2309.90.48 over quota)
levers.document: Entry under 2309.90.24 or 2309.90.44 while the quota is open. The quota is 7,399,700 kg a year in total, with at least 5,470,323 kg for Ireland, 1,782,618 kg for New Zealand, 83,914 kg for the United Kingdom and 56,699 kg for Australia (Additional U.S. note 2 to Chapter 23). Goods of Mexico cannot be entered in this quota; they enter free under USMCA.
levers.caveat: Once the quota is filled, the same feed pays 80.4¢/kg + 6.4% (2309.90.28, 2309.90.48). Check CBP's quota status before shipping.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty: a ruling fixes the line before the goods arrive — pet food vs. other feed, "mixed feed" (6% grain rule), milk content over or under 10%
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the classification decides the rate — especially 2309.90 (Free mixed feeds vs. 1.4%–80.4¢/kg + 6.4% other preparations)
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the product, its ingredients by weight and how it is put up.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different formula may need its own.

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods (or what you make from them) are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid on the imported goods
levers.appliesTo: Imported feed ingredients or pet food that are exported, destroyed, or used to make goods that are exported
levers.document: A drawback claim filed with CBP, with records that link the import to the export or destruction.
levers.caveat: Claims have deadlines and record-keeping rules. Antidumping and countervailing duties (such as those on Chinese lysine) are never refunded, and milk-based feed that paid the over-quota rate qualifies only for unused-merchandise drawback (19 CFR 191.3(b) and (c)).

rules.title: Food facility registration: the foreign plant that makes, packs or holds animal food must be registered with FDA
Prior notice: file it before every shipment of food for animals arrives (since October 1, 2026, mail shipments also need the mail tracking number)
Foreign Supplier Verification Program: the U.S. importer must verify that each foreign supplier of animal food meets U.S. safety standards

citations.label: FDA: FSMA final rule on FSVP

rules.title: Preventive controls for animal food: the maker follows FDA good manufacturing practice and a written food safety plan

citations.label: FDA: FSMA final rule for preventive controls for animal food

rules.title: Labels: product name, net quantity, manufacturer or distributor, and ingredients in order of weight; states also regulate pet food and feed labels
BSE feed rules: most mammalian protein may not be fed to cattle and other ruminants, and high-risk cattle material may not be used in any animal food
Import Alert 71-04: food for animals, including pet treats and chews, from listed firms is detained without examination for Salmonella (updated August 31, 2026)

Import Alert 99-29: vegetable protein products from China (corn gluten meal, soy meal, rice and wheat gluten and others) are detained without examination for melamine unless the firm is on the green list
Meat and bone meal, fish meal and other processed animal protein, and feed or pet food containing them: BSE restrictions, a foreign veterinary certificate and an APHIS import permit (VS Form 16-3)

No APHIS permit needed for some aquatic-animal material, plain rawhide chews and products whose only animal ingredient is lactose; fish meal and processed animal protein still need one (guidelines updated September 3, 2026)

groups.note: Corn gluten feed and meal, beet pulp and distillers' grains are FDA-regulated feed ingredients. Corn gluten meal from China is on FDA Import Alert 99-29 (melamine).

groups.note: Soybean meal is an FDA-regulated feed ingredient. Soy meal from China is on FDA Import Alert 99-29 (melamine).

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on pet food?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on pet food
faqs.answer: Dog and cat food put up for retail sale (2309.10) has a Free base rate, so the tariff is the extra duty for the country of origin. Since July 24, 2026 that is 12.5% for Thailand and Vietnam, 10% for Indonesia, Cambodia and Malaysia, 10% in total for EU countries, 37.5% for China (25% + 12.5%) and Brazil. USMCA-qualifying pet food from Canada and Mexico enters free. The U.S. imported $2.40B of retail dog and cat food in 2025.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on pet food and feed from Canada?
faqs.answer: Not if it qualifies for USMCA: qualifying goods pay no base rate and are exempt from the 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian products (9903.05.93). Goods that don't qualify pay their base rate plus 10% of value (9903.05.29). The 35% IEEPA duty ended February 24, 2026. Over-quota milk-based feed is the exception: free only within Canada's 696.9 t USMCA quota for 2026. Canada shipped $1.82B of Chapter 23 goods in 2025, mostly canola meal ($1.0B) and feed and pet food ($615M).

faqs.question: What is the tariff on pet food from Thailand?
faqs.answer: 12.5% of value since July 24, 2026: the base rate on dog and cat food is Free and Thailand is one of the 60 economies in the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.77). The 2025 reciprocal tariff ended on February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that followed expired July 23, 2026. Thailand supplied $1.04B of pet food and feed in 2025, up 21%.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on pet food and animal feed from China?
searchedAs: china tariff on prepared animal feed
china tariff on residues and waste from the food industries
faqs.answer: 37.5% of value on dog and cat food and most feed preparations: +25% from Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) plus +12.5% from the 2026 action (9903.05.31). Lines on List 4A, such as milk- and egg-based feed and cottonseed cake, pay 20% plus their base rate. Feed-grade lysine from China also owes antidumping and countervailing duties since September 2026, and FDA detains Chinese vegetable proteins such as corn gluten and soy meal under Import Alert 99-29 unless the firm is cleared. Imports from China fell 43% to $156M in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for pet food, dog food and cat food?
searchedAs: hs code for dry dog food
hs code for wet pet food
faqs.answer: Dog or cat food put up for retail sale is 2309.10: 2309.10.00.10 for food in airtight containers (canned or pouched wet food) and 2309.10.00.90 for the rest, such as dry kibble. Both have a Free base rate. Food for other pets put up for retail sale is 2309.90.10.15, and bird seed 2309.90.10.05, also Free.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for animal feed?
faqs.answer: Prepared animal feed is heading 2309. Mixed feeds with at least 6% grain are 2309.90.10 (Free), split into poultry, dairy cattle, other cattle, swine and other livestock feed. Feed containing milk is 2309.90.22 to 2309.90.48 (7.5% in quota, 80.4¢/kg + 6.4% above it), feed containing egg 2309.90.60 (1.9%), and other preparations 2309.90.70 and 2309.90.95 (1.4%). Feed ingredients such as soybean meal (2304), canola meal (2306.41) and fish meal (2301.20) have their own headings.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for animal feed supplements and additives?
searchedAs: hs code for animal feed supplements
hs code for animal feed additives
faqs.answer: Premixes and supplements made for animal feeding are usually 2309.90.70 (with a basis of vitamin B12) or 2309.90.95 (other), both 1.4%. A single chemical such as an amino acid or vitamin is normally classified in Chapter 29 instead. Feed-grade lysine from China owes antidumping and countervailing duties whether it enters as lysine or in a premix; the orders name 2922.41, 2309.90.70 and 2309.90.95.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and duty for soybean meal?
faqs.answer: 2304.00.00: soybean oilcake and meal, 0.45¢/kg (about $4.50 a tonne), with statistical lines for certified organic (.10) and other (.90). The U.S. imported $500M in 2025, up 27%, from Canada ($109M), Togo ($79M), Türkiye ($73M), Nigeria ($64M) and India ($37M). On top of the base rate, Türkiye and Nigeria pay +12.5% Section 301 and India +10%; Togo, outside the 60 economies, pays only the base rate, and USMCA-qualifying Canadian meal is free.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for fish meal?
searchedAs: hs code of fish meal powder
faqs.answer: 2301.20: flours, meals and pellets of fish or crustaceans, split into herring or pilchard meal (2301.20.00.10) and other (2301.20.00.90). The base rate is Free; the Section 301 duty for the country applies — Chile ($76M of fish and meat meal in 2025) pays 12.5% even with an FTA claim. Fish meal also needs a USDA APHIS import permit.

faqs.question: Can I bring pet food into the U.S.?
searchedAs: can i bring pet food into the us
bringing pet food into the us
faqs.answer: From Canada, travelers can bring pet food, chews and treats in unopened retail packaging — up to 50 lb per vehicle by land or 20 lb per family by air — and raw or dried items must be labeled a product of Canada or the U.S. Commercial shipments need FDA prior notice, a registered foreign facility and the importer's Foreign Supplier Verification Program; pet food made with meat, poultry or fish ingredients may also need a USDA APHIS import permit.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on lysine?
faqs.answer: On feed-grade lysine from China, yes: since September 2026 Commerce requires antidumping cash deposits of 73.37% to 139.65% (139.65% for the China-wide entity) and countervailing deposits of 48.21% to 82.11%, on top of the regular duties. The orders cover lysine in premixes and concentrates too (only the lysine part), including entries under 2309.90.70 and 2309.90.95.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import pet food and animal feed from?
faqs.answer: $5.42B of Chapter 23 goods in 2025. Canada supplied $1.82B (mostly canola meal and feed) and Thailand $1.04B (almost all pet food); then Indonesia ($227M), Mexico ($175M), China ($156M), Germany ($147M), Cambodia ($139M), France ($135M) and Malaysia ($134M). Retail dog and cat food alone was $2.40B.
